1	"""An append-only page store with an in-memory ordered directory.
2	
3	Several :class:`PageStore` instances -- in one process or in several -- may
4	share the same root directory.  A coordination file next to ``pages.dat``
5	(``.pages.dat.lock``) is locked while the serial point is read or moved, so
6	the outcome of concurrent writers is equivalent to running their calls one
7	after another: each successful put/delete (and every operation of a successful
8	batch) gets a strictly increasing record sequence number, a failed or
9	unconfirmed call -- including a whole unconfirmed batch -- never consumes a
10	number, and readers always see a complete before/after state.
11	
12	Instances also survive ``fork`` (``os.fork`` and the multiprocessing ``fork``
13	start): a forked child keeps using the very objects it inherited, with no
14	rebuild or ``recover`` required.  Right after the fork the child drops the
15	lock file descriptor and threading primitives it copied from the parent --
16	which may carry a lock held by a thread the child never received -- and opens
17	its own fresh descriptor, so the child can only wait for storage operations
18	that a live parent thread or process is actually still holding; those are
19	released when the operation completes or the holder exits.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import contextlib
25	import fcntl
26	import json
27	import os
28	import threading
29	import weakref
30	from pathlib import Path
31	
32	__all__ = ["PageStore", "Snapshot"]
33	
34	PAGE_SIZE = 4096
35	LOG_FILE = "pages.dat"
36	LOCK_FILE = f".{LOG_FILE}.lock"
37	
38	# --------------------------------------------------------------------- fork
39	#
40	# A forked child inherits every PageStore's coordination-file descriptor and
41	# gate lock.  The descriptor is a duplicate of the parent's open file
42	# description: if a parent thread held the flock at fork time, that lock is
43	# owned by a thread the child never received -- a child that kept using the
44	# inherited descriptor could block on it forever, and the inherited RLock may
45	# look held by a thread that does not exist in the child either.  The
46	# at-fork child hook resets every live instance before user code runs again;
47	# flock is tied to the open file description (not the pid), so closing the
48	# child's duplicate never disturbs a lock the parent genuinely still holds,
49	# while any lock of a process that exits is released by the kernel.
50	
51	_INSTANCES: "set[weakref.ReferenceType[PageStore]]" = set()
52	_REGISTRY_LOCK = threading.RLock()
53	
54	
55	def _drop_instance(ref: "weakref.ReferenceType[PageStore]") -> None:
56	    with _REGISTRY_LOCK:
57	        _INSTANCES.discard(ref)
58	
59	
60	def _before_fork() -> None:
61	    # Held across the fork so the registry cannot change underneath the
62	    # single thread that survives in the child.
63	    _REGISTRY_LOCK.acquire()
64	
65	
66	def _after_fork_parent() -> None:
67	    _REGISTRY_LOCK.release()
68	
69	
70	def _after_fork_child() -> None:
71	    global _REGISTRY_LOCK
72	    # The copied lock may appear owned by a thread that stayed in the parent;
73	    # start with a fresh, uncontended one instead of trying to release it.
74	    _REGISTRY_LOCK = threading.RLock()
75	    for ref in list(_INSTANCES):
76	        store = ref()
77	        if store is not None:
78	            store._reset_after_fork()
79	
80	
81	if hasattr(os, "register_at_fork"):
82	    os.register_at_fork(before=_before_fork,
83	                        after_in_parent=_after_fork_parent,
84	                        after_in_child=_after_fork_child)
85	
86	
87	class Snapshot:
88	    """A read-only view of a store's serial-point state fixed at capture time.
89	
90	    The view keeps its own in-memory copy, so later puts, deletes, recovery
91	    and compaction of the originating :class:`PageStore` never affect it, and
92	    concurrent writers in other processes cannot either.
93	    """
94	
95	    def __init__(self, live: dict[str, str], pages: int, records: int) -> None:
96	        self._live = dict(live)
97	        self._stats = {"pages": pages, "records": records, "keys": len(live)}
98	
99	    def get(self, key: str) -> str | None:
100	        return self._live.get(key)
101	
102	    def scan(self, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
103	        items = sorted(self._live.items())
104	        return [(k, v) for k, v in items
105	                if (start is None or k >= start) and (end is None or k < end)]
106	
107	    def stats(self) -> dict:
108	        return dict(self._stats)
109	
110	
111	class PageStore:
112	    """An append-only page store rooted at ``root``.
113	
114	    Multiple instances pointing at the same directory, including instances in
115	    different processes, coordinate through a lock file so that their
116	    interleaved calls have the same result as a serial ordering.
117	    """
118	
119	    def __init__(self, root: str | Path) -> None:
120	        self.directory = Path(root)
121	        self.path = self.directory / LOG_FILE
122	        self._lock_path = self.directory / LOCK_FILE
123	        # Serialises this instance's own locked sections (also against other
124	        # instances in the same process via the file lock) and guards the
125	        # cached serial-point state.
126	        self._gate = threading.RLock()
127	        self._lock_fd: int | None = None
128	        # The pid this instance has been prepared for; it differs after a
129	        # fork (see _after_fork_child / _reset_after_fork).
130	        self._pid = os.getpid()
131	        # Cached serial point: live directory, next sequence number (= number
132	        # of confirmed records), offset just past those records, and the
133	        # identity of the file they were read from.
134	        self._live: dict[str, str] | None = None
135	        self._seq = 0
136	        self._end = 0
137	        self._identity: tuple[int, int, int, int, int] | None = None
138	        with _REGISTRY_LOCK:
139	            _INSTANCES.add(weakref.ref(self, _drop_instance))
140	
141	    def _reset_after_fork(self) -> None:
142	        """Detach this copied instance from the forking process's resources.
143	
144	        Runs in the child immediately after a fork (and lazily via
145	        :meth:`_ensure_pid` if the hook somehow did not run).  The inherited
146	        coordination-file descriptor is closed without being unlocked and the
147	        gate is replaced: the descriptor shares the parent's open file
148	        description and the gate may be held by a thread the child never
149	        received.  The cached serial point is dropped too, since the parent
150	        (or a sibling) may move it while the child is alive; the first call
151	        rebuilds it under the child's own coordination lock.
152	        """
153	        fd = self._lock_fd
154	        self._lock_fd = None
155	        if fd is not None:
156	            # Closing this duplicate never releases a lock the parent still
157	            # holds: an flock lives on the shared open file description and is
158	            # released only once *all* its duplicates are closed (the parent
159	            # keeps its own).  It must not be unlocked explicitly, since
160	            # LOCK_UN on any duplicate would release the parent's live lock.
161	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
162	                os.close(fd)
163	        self._gate = threading.RLock()
164	        self._live = None
165	        self._seq = 0
166	        self._end = 0
167	        self._identity = None
168	        self._pid = os.getpid()
169	
170	    def _ensure_pid(self) -> None:
171	        """Repair the instance if it finds itself in a different process.
172	
173	        Belt-and-braces behind the ``register_at_fork`` hook: an instance
174	        created before the fork module was wired up, or a fork path that
175	        bypassed the hook, is repaired on its first locked section.  This is
176	        only safe to call when no other thread in *this* process can be
177	        inside the instance (e.g. the single surviving forking thread).
178	        """
179	        if self._pid != os.getpid():
180	            self._reset_after_fork()
181	
182	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ init
183	
184	    def init(self) -> None:
185	        self.directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
186	        with self._locked(exclusive=True, require=False):
187	            # Install a *fresh empty inode* rather than truncating the old one.
188	            # A reset is a serial state change on equal footing with a compaction:
189	            # other instances detect a new inode (independent of the file's new
190	            # length) and rebuild from an empty image, so pre-reset writes can
191	            # neither be resurrected from a long-lived cache nor shadow records
192	            # appended after the reset -- even when the new file grows as long
193	            # as or longer than the old one.  The temp file is fsynced and the
194	            # swap is followed by a directory fsync, so an interrupted init
195	            # leaves either the complete old file or the complete empty one.
196	            tmp = self.directory / f".{LOG_FILE}.init.tmp"
197	            try:
198	                with tmp.open("wb") as handle:
199	                    handle.flush()
200	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
201	                os.replace(tmp, self.path)
202	                dirfd = os.open(self.directory, os.O_RDONLY)
203	                try:
204	                    os.fsync(dirfd)
205	                finally:
206	                    os.close(dirfd)
207	            except BaseException:
208	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
209	                    tmp.unlink()
210	                # The old file may or may not still be the one the cache was
211	                # built from; force a full rescan on the next operation.
212	                self._invalidate()
213	                raise
214	            self._invalidate()
215	            self._resync()
216	
217	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- locking
218	
219	    @contextlib.contextmanager
220	    def _locked(self, exclusive: bool, require: bool = True):
221	        """Hold the cross-process coordination lock for one serial operation."""
222	        self._ensure_pid()
223	        with self._gate:
224	            # Fail before touching the coordination file: a missing root, a
225	            # root that is a file, or an absent pages.dat must not create
226	            # anything (and would otherwise raise NotADirectoryError).  init is
227	            # the one call allowed to create pages.dat itself.
228	            if require:
229	                self._require_store()
230	            if self._lock_fd is None or os.fstat(self._lock_fd).st_nlink == 0:
231	                # The coordination file only serialises access; it is never
232	                # counted as a record or treated as data by compact.  If it
233	                # was removed out from under us, reopen the current path so
234	                # everyone converges on one lock inode again.
235	                if self._lock_fd is not None:
236	                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
237	                        os.close(self._lock_fd)
238	                self._lock_fd = os.open(
239	                    self._lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_CLOEXEC,
240	                    0o600)
241	            fcntl.flock(
242	                self._lock_fd,
243	                fcntl.LOCK_EX if exclusive else fcntl.LOCK_SH)
244	            try:
245	                yield
246	            finally:
247	                fcntl.flock(self._lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
248	
249	    def _require_store(self) -> None:
250	        if not self.directory.is_dir() or not self.path.is_file():
251	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"no store at {self.path}; run init first")
252	
253	    def _identity_of(self) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
254	        stat = self.path.stat()
255	        return (stat.st_dev, stat.st_ino, stat.st_size,
256	                stat.st_mtime_ns, stat.st_ctime_ns)
257	
258	    def _invalidate(self) -> None:
259	        self._live = None
260	        self._identity = None
261	
262	    @staticmethod
263	    def _record_at(data: bytes, offset: int) -> tuple[int, dict] | None:
264	        """Parse one record at ``offset``.
265	
266	        A record is a four-byte big-endian length prefix followed by UTF-8
267	        bytes encoding a JSON object.  A bare record's payload is 1..4096
268	        bytes and its ``op`` is ``"put"`` or ``"delete"``; a ``put`` record
269	        carries a string ``value`` and a ``delete`` does not.  A batch
270	        record's ``op`` is ``"batch"`` and its ``ops`` is a non-empty list
271	        of those same put/delete objects; a batch frame may span several
272	        pages, so its payload is bounded only by the declared length rather
273	        than one page.  A ``delete`` ignores its ``value`` and bare ops
274	        ignore every other field.  Anything else -- a partial prefix, a
275	        declared length past EOF, a bare-record length outside 1..4096, bad
276	        UTF-8 or JSON, a scalar/array payload, an unknown op, a malformed
277	        batch, or a missing/invalid ``key``/``value`` -- is a break in the
278	        stream rather than a record, so callers treat it exactly like a
279	        half-written tail and never let a ``KeyError``/``TypeError`` escape.
280	        Returns the boundary just past the record and its decoded object, or
281	        ``None``.
282	        """
283	        size = len(data)
284	        if offset + 4 > size:
285	            return None
286	        rec_size = int.from_bytes(data[offset:offset + 4], "big")
287	        end = offset + 4 + rec_size
288	        if rec_size < 1 or end > size:
289	            return None
290	        try:
291	            decoded = json.loads(data[offset + 4:end].decode("utf-8"))
292	        except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
293	            return None
294	        if not isinstance(decoded, dict):
295	            return None
296	        op = decoded.get("op")
297	        if op == "batch":
298	            ops = decoded.get("ops")
299	            if not isinstance(ops, list) or not ops:
300	                return None
301	            for item in ops:
302	                if not PageStore._valid_item(item):
303	                    return None
304	            return end, decoded
305	        if op not in ("put", "delete"):
306	            return None
307	        # Bare put/delete records stay bounded to one page.
308	        if rec_size > PAGE_SIZE:
309	            return None
310	        key = decoded.get("key")
311	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
312	            return None
313	        if op == "put" and not isinstance(decoded.get("value"), str):
314	            return None
315	        return end, decoded
316	
317	    @staticmethod
318	    def _valid_item(item: object) -> bool:
319	        """Whether ``item`` is an exact put/delete operation dictionary."""
320	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
321	            return False
322	        op = item.get("op")
323	        if op == "put":
324	            if set(item) != {"op", "key", "value"}:
325	                return False
326	            return isinstance(item["key"], str) and bool(item["key"]) \
327	                and isinstance(item["value"], str)
328	        if op == "delete":
329	            if set(item) != {"op", "key"}:
330	                return False
331	            return isinstance(item["key"], str) and bool(item["key"])
332	        return False
333	
334	    @staticmethod
335	    def _apply(live: dict[str, str], decoded: dict) -> int:
336	        """Replay one decoded record into ``live``; return its record count.
337	
338	        A bare put/delete counts once; a batch applies its operations in
339	        order without merging and counts one per operation.
340	        """
341	        if decoded["op"] != "batch":
342	            if decoded["op"] == "put":
343	                live[decoded["key"]] = decoded["value"]
344	            else:
345	                live.pop(decoded["key"], None)
346	            return 1
347	        for item in decoded["ops"]:
348	            if item["op"] == "put":
349	                live[item["key"]] = item["value"]
350	            else:
351	                live.pop(item["key"], None)
352	        return len(decoded["ops"])
353	
354	    @classmethod
355	    def _record_past(cls, data: bytes, offset: int) -> bool:
356	        """Whether a valid record starts at any later offset past ``offset``.
357	
358	        Only a frame that satisfies the full record rule can be evidence of
359	        mid-file corruption; a scalar JSON value or an invalid object buried in
360	        the damaged region proves nothing.  The first offsets tried immediately
361	        after the break also cover the case where the frame's own declared
362	        length runs past EOF (its whole payload region is searched).
363	
364	        Every candidate whose declared length fits is judged by the very same
365	        record rule the continuous reader applies, so a reordered ``op``
366	        member, any amount of JSON whitespace ahead of the object, a
367	        Unicode-escaped member name and a batch payload spanning several
368	        pages are all recognised exactly as they are in a clean prefix.  The
369	        one cheap pre-check -- a valid record's payload is a JSON object, so
370	        its first non-whitespace byte must be ``{`` -- keeps the scan O(n)
371	        without rejecting anything the full parse would accept.
372	        """
373	        size = len(data)
374	        for start in range(offset + 1, size - 3):
375	            rec_size = int.from_bytes(data[start:start + 4], "big")
376	            end = start + 4 + rec_size
377	            if rec_size < 1 or end > size:
378	                continue
379	            pos = start + 4
380	            while pos < end and data[pos] in b" \t\n\r":
381	                pos += 1
382	            if pos >= end or data[pos] != 0x7B:  # '{'
383	                continue
384	            if cls._record_at(data, start) is not None:
385	                return True
386	        return False
387	
388	    def _scan_from(self, data: bytes, offset: int,
389	                   live: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[int, int]:
390	        """Replay whole records from ``offset`` into ``live``; return (end, count).
391	
392	        Stops at the first boundary that is not a whole, valid record; the
393	        caller decides whether the remaining bytes are a half-written tail or
394	        mid-file corruption.
395	        """
396	        size = len(data)
397	        count = 0
398	        while offset < size:
399	            parsed = self._record_at(data, offset)
400	            if parsed is None:
401	                break
402	            offset, decoded = parsed
403	            count += self._apply(live, decoded)
404	        return offset, count
405	
406	    def _resync(self) -> None:
407	        """Rebuild or extend the cached serial point from the current page file.
408	
409	        Must be called while holding the coordination lock.  When the file has
410	        been replaced (another instance compacted) the whole image is read;
411	        otherwise only bytes past the previously confirmed offset are replayed,
412	        which also discards a half-written tail left by a crashed writer.
413	        """
414	        self._require_store()
415	        identity = self._identity_of()
416	        data = self.path.read_bytes()
417	        replaced = self._live is None or self._identity is None or \
418	            identity[:2] != self._identity[:2]
419	        if replaced or len(data) < self._end:
420	            # New file (another instance compacted) or an externally
421	            # truncated inode: rebuild the serial point from the beginning.
422	            live: dict[str, str] = {}
423	            offset, count = self._scan_from(data, 0, live)
424	            self._live = live
425	            self._seq = count
426	            self._end = offset
427	        else:
428	            # Same inode: replay only what other processes appended beyond the
429	            # last confirmed boundary (including an earlier half-write).
430	            offset, count = self._scan_from(data, self._end, self._live)
431	            self._seq += count
432	            self._end = offset
433	        self._identity = identity
434	
435	    def _state(self, exclusive: bool) -> tuple[dict[str, str], int, int]:
436	        with self._locked(exclusive=exclusive):
437	            self._resync()
438	            # Copy so callers can never mutate the serial-point directory.
439	            return dict(self._live), self._seq, self._identity[2]  # type: ignore[index]
440	
441	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- writing
442	
443	    @staticmethod
444	    def _encode(record: dict) -> bytes:
445	        payload = json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
446	        return len(payload).to_bytes(4, "big") + payload
447	
448	    def _append_record(self, record: dict, count: int,
449	                       expected: dict[str, str | None] | None = None,
450	                       expect_range: "tuple[dict[str, str], str | None, str | None] | None" = None
451	                       ) -> list[int] | None:
452	        """Append one already-validated frame covering ``count`` records.
453	
454	        Returns the consecutive sequence numbers assigned to those records,
455	        starting at one past the number of confirmed records.  A bare
456	        put/delete passes ``count == 1``; a batch frame passes the length of
457	        its operation list, and the whole frame lands -- or is rolled back --
458	        as one serial point, so a crash keeps either all of it or none.
459	
460	        When ``expected`` is given, the frame is appended only if every
461	        condition holds at the serial point: a string must equal the key's
462	        current live value exactly, ``None`` requires the key to be absent
463	        (a deleted key is absent; an empty-string value is not).  When
464	        ``expect_range`` is given, it carries a required live mapping and a
465	        half-open ``[start, end)`` range, and the frame is appended only when
466	        the keys currently live inside that range equal the mapping exactly
467	        -- same keys, same values, in any order: an inserted key, a deleted
468	        key or a changed value all fail the condition, while keys outside the
469	        range are irrelevant.  A failed condition returns ``None`` instead: no
470	        number is consumed and the page file is left byte-for-byte untouched
471	        -- in particular a half-written tail is not truncated, since nothing
472	        was committed.  A half-written tail never takes part in the
473	        comparison, since only confirmed records are replayed into the
474	        serial point.
475	        """
476	        frame = self._encode(record)
477	        with self._locked(exclusive=True):
478	            # Another process may have appended or compacted since we last
479	            # synced; bring the serial point up to date first.
480	            self._resync()
481	            assert self._live is not None and self._identity is not None
482	            size = self._identity[2]
483	            if size - self._end > 0:
484	                data = self.path.read_bytes()
485	                if self._record_past(data, self._end):
486	                    # A complete, valid record exists beyond the unparseable
487	                    # region: the file is corrupt in the middle.  Never
488	                    # overwrite or skip those records; leave the file
489	                    # byte-for-byte untouched.
490	                    raise RuntimeError("corrupt_middle")
491	            if expected:
492	                # Conditions are checked against the serial point just
493	                # established, inside the same locked section as the commit,
494	                # so check-and-commit is one serial operation.  Live values
495	                # are always strings, so ``None`` from ``get`` means absent.
496	                for key, want in expected.items():
497	                    current = self._live.get(key)
498	                    if want is None:
499	                        if current is not None:
500	                            return None
501	                    elif current != want:
502	                        return None
503	            if expect_range is not None:
504	                wanted, rstart, rend = expect_range
505	                # Exact-equality check of the mapping of every key currently
506	                # live inside [start, end): same key set, same values.  Dict
507	                # equality ignores ordering, so the caller's key order is
508	                # irrelevant; a size mismatch catches an inserted or deleted
509	                # key.  Keys outside the range never enter the comparison.
510	                actual = {key: value for key, value in self._live.items()
511	                          if (rstart is None or key >= rstart)
512	                          and (rend is None or key < rend)}
513	                if actual != wanted:
514	                    return None
515	            try:
516	                with self.path.open("r+b") as handle:
517	                    # Cut at the confirmed boundary so a half-written tail
518	                    # left by a crashed (unconfirmed) writer is overwritten
519	                    # rather than sealed in front of the new record.
520	                    if size - self._end > 0:
521	                        handle.truncate(self._end)
522	                    handle.seek(self._end)
523	                    handle.write(frame)
524	                    handle.flush()
525	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
526	            except OSError:
527	                # Unconfirmed call: best-effort rollback to the confirmed
528	                # boundary so it occupies no sequence number and stays
529	                # invisible, then drop the cache for a fresh scan.
530	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
531	                    with self.path.open("r+b") as rollback:
532	                        rollback.truncate(self._end)
533	                        rollback.flush()
534	                        os.fsync(rollback.fileno())
535	                self._invalidate()
536	                raise
537	            # Confirmed: the append is now part of the serial point.
538	            first = self._seq + 1
539	            self._apply(self._live, record)
540	            self._seq += count
541	            self._end += len(frame)
542	            try:
543	                self._identity = self._identity_of()
544	            except OSError:
545	                self._invalidate()
546	            return list(range(first, first + count))
547	
548	    @staticmethod
549	    def _check_key(key: object) -> None:
550	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
551	            raise ValueError("key must be a non-empty string")
552	
553	    def put(self, key: str, value: str) -> int:
554	        self._check_key(key)
555	        if not isinstance(value, str):
556	            raise ValueError("value must be a string")
557	        record = {"op": "put", "key": key, "value": value}
558	        payload_size = len(self._encode(record)) - 4
559	        if payload_size > PAGE_SIZE:
560	            raise ValueError(
561	                f"record exceeds one page ({payload_size} > {PAGE_SIZE})")
562	        return self._append_record(record, 1)[0]
563	
564	    def delete(self, key: str) -> int:
565	        self._check_key(key)
566	        return self._append_record({"op": "delete", "key": key}, 1)[0]
567	
568	    @classmethod
569	    def _normalize_operations(cls, operations: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
570	        """Validate a batch operation list wholesale and normalise it.
571	
572	        Raises ``ValueError`` for any malformed element or oversized single
573	        operation; nothing is stored and no sequence number is consumed.
574	        """
575	        if not isinstance(operations, list) or not operations:
576	            raise ValueError("operations must be a non-empty list")
577	        normalized: list[dict] = []
578	        for item in operations:
579	            if not cls._valid_item(item):
580	                raise ValueError(
581	                    "each operation must be a dict with op 'put' "
582	                    "(keys op, key, value) or 'delete' (keys op, key); "
583	                    "key must be a non-empty string and value a string")
584	            record = {"op": item["op"], "key": item["key"]}
585	            if item["op"] == "put":
586	                record["value"] = item["value"]
587	            if len(cls._encode(record)) - 4 > PAGE_SIZE:
588	                raise ValueError(
589	                    "an operation in the batch exceeds the one-record "
590	                    f"size limit ({PAGE_SIZE} bytes)")
591	            normalized.append(record)
592	        return normalized
593	
594	    def write_batch(self, operations: list[dict]) -> list[int]:
595	        """Atomically append a non-empty batch of put/delete operations.
596	
597	        Each element is an operation dict: a put has exactly the keys
598	        ``op``, ``key`` and ``value``; a delete has exactly ``op`` and
599	        ``key``.  Keys are non-empty strings and values are strings; every
600	        single operation must fit the existing one-record size limit.  The
601	        whole list is validated -- without touching the page file or
602	        consuming a sequence number -- before anything is stored.
603	
604	        The batch takes effect as one serial point, operations applied in
605	        input order (duplicate keys are not merged and deleting a missing
606	        key still takes a number).  It may span several pages and is stored
607	        as one frame, so a failed write or a process crash leaves either the
608	        entire batch or none of it: an unconfirmed batch is a half-written
609	        tail on reopen and is discarded by the next write or ``recover``.
610	        Returns the operations' consecutive sequence numbers, starting at
611	        one past the current number of confirmed records.
612	
613	        Raises ``ValueError`` for any malformed batch or oversized
614	        operation, ``FileNotFoundError`` when the root is missing, points
615	        at a file, or ``pages.dat`` is absent, ``RuntimeError
616	        ("corrupt_middle")`` when damage precedes complete records (the
617	        file is left untouched), and ``OSError`` on other read/write
618	        failures.
619	        """
620	        normalized = self._normalize_operations(operations)
621	        return self._append_record({"op": "batch", "ops": normalized},
622	                                   len(normalized))
623	
624	    def write_batch_if(self, expected: dict[str, str | None],
625	                       operations: list[dict]) -> list[int] | None:
626	        """Commit a batch only if every condition in ``expected`` holds.
627	
628	        ``expected`` maps keys to the state they must be in at the serial
629	        point: a string requires the key's current live value to be exactly
630	        equal, ``None`` requires the key to be absent (a deleted key is
631	        absent; an empty-string value is not).  Condition keys need not
632	        appear in ``operations``, and an empty ``expected`` dict commits
633	        unconditionally.  Both arguments are validated wholesale first --
634	        ``expected`` must be a dict with non-empty string keys and
635	        string-or-``None`` values, and ``operations`` follows the exact
636	        ``write_batch`` rules -- so any ``ValueError`` is raised before the
637	        store is touched, ahead of every storage error, and leaves the page
638	        file and sequence numbers unchanged.
639	
640	        The condition check and the commit are one serial operation, sharing
641	        the coordination lock with every other write, reset, recovery and
642	        compaction across instances, threads and processes on this machine:
643	        two concurrent calls that both read the same old value and each try
644	        to replace it cannot both succeed.  If any condition fails the call
645	        returns ``None``: no sequence number is consumed and the page file
646	        is left byte-for-byte untouched, including any half-written tail a
647	        crashed writer left behind.  On success the batch lands exactly like
648	        a ``write_batch`` frame (conditions are not recorded and never count
649	        toward the record total) and the operations' consecutive sequence
650	        numbers are returned, starting at one past the number of confirmed
651	        records at that serial point.
652	
653	        Raises ``ValueError`` for any malformed argument,
654	        ``FileNotFoundError`` when the root is missing, points at a file, or
655	        ``pages.dat`` is absent (no storage path is created),
656	        ``RuntimeError("corrupt_middle")`` when damage precedes complete
657	        records -- even when a condition would have failed -- and
658	        ``OSError`` on other read/write failures.
659	        """
660	        if not isinstance(expected, dict):
661	            raise ValueError(
662	                "expected must be a dict mapping keys to their required "
663	                "current value (a string) or None (key must be absent)")
664	        for key, want in expected.items():
665	            self._check_key(key)
666	            if want is not None and not isinstance(want, str):
667	                raise ValueError("expected values must be strings or None")
668	        normalized = self._normalize_operations(operations)
669	        return self._append_record({"op": "batch", "ops": normalized},
670	                                   len(normalized), expected=dict(expected))
671	
672	    @staticmethod
673	    def _check_boundary(value: object, name: str) -> None:
674	        if value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
675	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a string or None")
676	
677	    def write_batch_if_range(self, expected: dict[str, str],
678	                             operations: list[dict],
679	                             start: str | None = None,
680	                             end: str | None = None) -> list[int] | None:
681	        """Commit a batch only if a whole key range matches ``expected``.
682	
683	        ``expected`` maps non-empty string keys to the string values that
684	        must be the *entire* live content of the half-open range
685	        ``[start, end)`` at the serial point: the keys currently live in the
686	        range must be exactly its keys with exactly its values.  Dict order
687	        is irrelevant; an empty ``expected`` requires the range to contain no
688	        live keys at all.  Bounds follow the ``scan`` rules: ``start`` is
689	        inclusive and ``end`` exclusive, either may be ``None`` for an open
690	        bound, an empty string is a legal bound, and ``start >= end``
691	        describes an empty range.  Every condition key must itself lie inside
692	        the range.
693	
694	        ``operations`` follows the exact ``write_batch`` rules and may touch
695	        keys outside the range; those writes never affect the comparison.
696	        All arguments are validated wholesale before the store is touched,
697	        so every ``ValueError`` is raised ahead of any storage error and
698	        leaves the page file and sequence numbers unchanged.
699	
700	        The comparison and the commit are one serial operation under the
701	        coordination lock, shared with every other write, reset, recovery
702	        and compaction across instances, threads and processes: a key
703	        inserted by a scan-then-check transaction blocks the commit.  An
704	        insertion, deletion or value change anywhere in the range fails the
705	        condition (returning ``None``, byte-for-byte untouched, half-written
706	        tail included); changes outside the range do not, and a key that
707	        changed and was later restored to its original state matches again.
708	        On success the frame lands exactly like a ``write_batch`` frame --
709	        conditions are neither recorded nor counted -- and the operations'
710	        consecutive sequence numbers are returned, starting at one past the
711	        number of confirmed records at that serial point.
712	
713	        Raises ``ValueError`` for any malformed argument (including a
714	        condition key outside the range), ``FileNotFoundError`` when the
715	        root is missing, points at a file, or ``pages.dat`` is absent (no
716	        storage path is created), ``RuntimeError("corrupt_middle")`` when
717	        damage precedes complete records -- even when the comparison would
718	        have failed -- and ``OSError`` on other read/write failures.
719	        """
720	        if not isinstance(expected, dict):
721	            raise ValueError(
722	                "expected must be a dict mapping the range's live keys to "
723	                "their required current string values; an empty dict "
724	                "requires the range to be empty")
725	        for key, want in expected.items():
726	            self._check_key(key)
727	            if not isinstance(want, str):
728	                raise ValueError("expected values must be strings")
729	        self._check_boundary(start, "start")
730	        self._check_boundary(end, "end")
731	        for key in expected:
732	            if (start is not None and key < start) or \
733	                    (end is not None and key >= end):
734	                raise ValueError(
735	                    f"condition key {key!r} lies outside the requested range")
736	        normalized = self._normalize_operations(operations)
737	        return self._append_record(
738	            {"op": "batch", "ops": normalized}, len(normalized),
739	            expect_range=(dict(expected), start, end))
740	
741	    # -------------------------------------------------------------- reading
742	
743	    def _live_state(self) -> dict[str, str]:
744	        return self._state(exclusive=False)[0]
745	
746	    def get(self, key: str) -> str | None:
747	        return self._live_state().get(key)
748	
749	    def scan(self, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
750	        live = self._live_state()
751	        items = sorted(live.items())
752	        return [(k, v) for k, v in items if (start is None or k >= start) and (end is None or k < end)]
753	
754	    def snapshot(self) -> Snapshot:
755	        """Capture the live key state at call time as an immutable read-only view.
756	
757	        The capture is taken under the coordination lock, so only the complete
758	        before/after state of any concurrent put, delete, recover or compact is
759	        ever seen.  Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` like the other read operations
760	        when the root is missing, points at a file, or ``pages.dat`` is absent.
761	        """
762	        with self._locked(exclusive=False):
763	            self._resync()
764	            assert self._live is not None and self._identity is not None
765	            pages = (self._identity[2] + PAGE_SIZE - 1) // PAGE_SIZE
766	            return Snapshot(self._live, pages, self._seq)
767	
768	    def stats(self) -> dict:
769	        live, seq, size = self._state(exclusive=False)
770	        return {"pages": (size + PAGE_SIZE - 1) // PAGE_SIZE,
771	                "records": seq, "keys": len(live)}
772	
773	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ compaction
774	
775	    def compact(self) -> dict:
776	        """Rewrite live key/value pairs as the fewest ascending ``put`` records.
777	
778	        Confirmed records are replayed strictly along length-prefix
779	        boundaries.  Old values and delete records are discarded; a
780	        half-written tail is discarded too.  The result is written to a
781	        temporary file and atomically swapped in, so an interrupted
782	        compaction leaves either the complete old file or the complete new
783	        one -- never a mixture.
784	
785	        The whole operation is one serial point: it is mutually exclusive with
786	        concurrent puts, deletes and recoveries (here or in other processes),
787	        and ``pages_before``, ``pages_after``, ``records_before``,
788	        ``records_after``, ``keys`` and ``discarded_tail_bytes`` all describe
789	        that same point.  Later appends number from the post-compaction record
790	        count.
791	
792	        Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` when the root is missing, points at a
793	        file, or ``pages.dat`` is absent; ``RuntimeError("corrupt_middle")``
794	        when a complete record can still be found past a damaged region (the
795	        file is left untouched); and ``OSError`` on read/write failures.
796	        """
797	        with self._locked(exclusive=True):
798	            self._resync()
799	            assert self._live is not None
800	            data = self.path.read_bytes()
801	            size = len(data)
802	            offset, records_before = 0, 0
803	            live: dict[str, str] = {}
804	            while offset < size:
805	                parsed = self._record_at(data, offset)
806	                if parsed is None:
807	                    break  # the continuous valid prefix ends here
808	                offset, decoded = parsed
809	                records_before += self._apply(live, decoded)
810	            if offset < size and self._record_past(data, offset):
811	                raise RuntimeError("corrupt_middle")  # leave the file untouched
812	            discarded = size - offset
813	            frames = [self._encode({"op": "put", "key": key, "value": live[key]})
814	                      for key in sorted(live)]
815	            pages_before = (size + PAGE_SIZE - 1) // PAGE_SIZE
816	            new_size = sum(map(len, frames))
817	            tmp = self.directory / f".{LOG_FILE}.compact.tmp"
818	            try:
819	                with tmp.open("wb") as handle:
820	                    handle.write(b"".join(frames))
821	                    handle.flush()
822	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
823	                os.replace(tmp, self.path)
824	                dirfd = os.open(self.directory, os.O_RDONLY)
825	                try:
826	                    os.fsync(dirfd)
827	                finally:
828	                    os.close(dirfd)
829	            except BaseException:
830	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
831	                    tmp.unlink()
832	                # The old file may or may not still be the one the cache was
833	                # built from; force a full rescan on the next operation.
834	                self._invalidate()
835	                raise
836	            # The atomic swap is the new serial point.
837	            self._live = dict(live)
838	            self._seq = len(frames)
839	            self._end = new_size
840	            self._identity = self._identity_of()
841	            records_after = len(frames)
842	            return {"pages_before": pages_before,
843	                    "pages_after": (new_size + PAGE_SIZE - 1) // PAGE_SIZE,
844	                    "records_before": records_before,
845	                    "records_after": records_after,
846	                    "keys": len(live),
847	                    "discarded_tail_bytes": discarded}
848	
849	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- recovery
850	
851	    def recover(self) -> dict:
852	        """Reopen the page file, dropping a half-written tail record.
853	
854	        Records are scanned strictly along length-prefix boundaries.  The first
855	        boundary that is not a whole, parseable record marks a half-written
856	        tail: scanning stops and every byte from that boundary on is removed, so
857	        later appends continue right after the last confirmed record.
858	
859	        If a complete record can still be re-synchronised past the stop offset,
860	        the damage is mid-file corruption rather than a half-written tail:
861	        ``RuntimeError("corrupt_middle")`` is raised and the file is left
862	        byte-for-byte untouched.
863	
864	        Recovery shares the serial point with writes, so only a confirmed tail
865	        is ever truncated and concurrent appends cannot race the cut.
866	        """
867	        with self._locked(exclusive=True):
868	            self._require_store()
869	            data = self.path.read_bytes()
870	            size = len(data)
871	            offset, records = 0, 0
872	            live: dict[str, str] = {}
873	            while offset < size:
874	                parsed = self._record_at(data, offset)
875	                if parsed is None:
876	                    break  # partial prefix, declared length past EOF/out of
877	                           # range, bad encoding/JSON, or an invalid payload
878	                offset, decoded = parsed
879	                records += self._apply(live, decoded)
880	            truncated = offset < size
881	            if truncated:
882	                if self._record_past(data, offset):
883	                    raise RuntimeError("corrupt_middle")
884	                with self.path.open("r+b") as handle:
885	                    handle.truncate(offset)
886	                    handle.flush()
887	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
888	            self._live = live
889	            self._seq = records
890	            self._end = offset
891	            self._identity = self._identity_of()
892	            return {"pages": (offset + PAGE_SIZE - 1) // PAGE_SIZE,
893	                    "records": records, "truncated": truncated}
894	
895	    # --------------------------------------------------------------- verify
896	
897	    def verify(self) -> dict:
898	        """Read-only check of the page file; never mutates the store."""
899	        result = {"status": "ok", "complete_records": 0, "valid_pages": 0,
900	                  "first_error_offset": None, "tail_partial_bytes": 0,
901	                  "scanned_end_offset": None, "error": None}
902	        if not self.directory.is_dir() or not self.path.is_file():
903	            result.update(status="error", error="invalid_path")
904	            return result
905	        with self._locked(exclusive=False):
906	            try:
907	                data = self.path.read_bytes()
908	            except OSError:
909	                result.update(status="error", error="read_error")
910	                return result
911	        size = len(data)
912	        result["scanned_end_offset"] = size
913	        offset = 0
914	        replay: dict[str, str] = {}
915	        while offset < size:
916	            parsed = self._record_at(data, offset)
917	            if parsed is None:
918	                break
919	            offset, decoded = parsed
920	            # A batch frame counts as one retained record per operation;
921	            # its wrapper metadata never counts.
922	            result["complete_records"] += self._apply(replay, decoded)
923	        result["valid_pages"] = offset // PAGE_SIZE
924	        if offset == size:
925	            return result
926	        if self._record_past(data, offset):
927	            result.update(status="corrupt_middle", error="corrupt_middle",
928	                          first_error_offset=offset)
929	        else:
930	            result.update(status="incomplete_tail", tail_partial_bytes=size - offset)
931	        return result
